newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Herzog to meet U.S. Jewish groups.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Herzog to meet U.S. Jewish groups.

text.p: German President Roman Herzog left Bonn on Wednesday for a four-day trip to the United States, where he is due to receive two prizes and meet Jewish leaders who have recently heaped criticism on his country.

Herzog was set to hold talks with U.S. Jewish leaders from two groups who have slammed Germany over the issues of compensation for eastern European Holocaust survivors and former war criminals who are receiving state pensions.

Herzog, whose office is largely ceremonial but who is seen as Germany's moral conscience, does not dodge difficult topics and last month won respect at home with a frank speech scolding politicians for a deadlock on key reforms.

The straight-talking Bavarian was due to meet members of the American Jewish Committee, which last week said that in the United States alone 3,377 pensions were sent each month to veterans of the armies of the Third Reich or their dependents.

The group also said that while Holocaust survivors in other parts of the world were eligible to receive German pensions, up to 20,000 survivors in eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union had never received any kind of pension from Bonn.

Herzog will also meet Edgar Bronfman, president of the World Jewish Congress, which last December called on Germany to publish the names of former members of Adolf Hitler's Waffen SS elite forces who live in Britain and the United States and who receive disability pensions.
Herzog was also set to receive a statesman of the year award jointly with Czech President Vaclav Havel at the Institute for East-West studies.
The award honours both men for their work towards the historic declaration of post-war reconciliation signed earlier this year between Germany and the Czech Republic.

Herzog was also due to receive the Joseph Prize for Human Rights from U.S. human rights organisation, the Anti-Defamation League, for fighting racism in Germany and promoting relations between Germans and Jews.
He ends his visit to the U.S. on Sunday when he is due to receive an honorary doctorate from the legal faculty at the Notre Dame University, Indiana.
